function: Learns joint task offloading and resource allocation (CPU frequency, bandwidth, uplink and downlink transmit power) for UAV-to-MEC-server air-to-ground links, minimizing weighted delay and energy (p. 5-6).
system: 20 UAVs and 5 MEC servers, A2G/G2A OFDMA links, 20 MHz, Shannon rate with distance path loss; antennas and carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (p. 4, 9).
method: DDPG-MHSA: deep deterministic policy gradient with multi-head self-attention actor-critic encoder-decoder; reinforcement learning, 6000 training episodes in simulation (p. 6-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: 1000 m x 1000 m area, random UAV and server positions, distance path loss, noise 1e-13; no standard channel model or dataset (p. 4, 9).
test_conditions: Trained with 20 UAVs and tasks of 0.9-1.1 Gcycles, 300-500 kbits; tested with 10-30 UAVs and tasks of 0.7-1.4 Gcycles, 100-800 kbits (p. 11).
baselines: Non-learned: ALE, ROE random offloading, THOA genetic heuristic; learned: HPPO [45], HSAC [46] (DRL) (p. 10).
metrics: Average total cost (weighted delay and energy), episode reward, running time in seconds, generalization to UAV count and task attributes (p. 10-11).
complexity: Order of complexity of actor and critic networks and training, Eqs. (52)-(54), plus measured average running time 0.010-0.011 s (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 4: "v denotes the path loss factor"
q2_support: p. 11: "the DDPG-MHSA model trained on 20 UAVs to solve the JTORA-MUMS problems with 10 to 30 UAVs"
q3_support: p. 11: "the DRL-based methods (DDPG-MHSA, HPPO, and HSAC) outperform the heuristic method THOA and the traditional methods ALE and ROE in terms of solution quality"

notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Borderline eligibility: the task is MEC offloading, above the physical layer, but the policy also sets bandwidth and uplink and downlink transmit power of the aerial links (p. 6, Eqs. 21-23), so the aerial-link carve-out of above_phy applies and the area is 6; the reviewer should confirm. q1 = 0: channel gain is a distance power law only (p. 4), no standardized model or measured data. q2 = 1: one model trained with 20 UAVs is tested with other UAV counts and wider task ranges, with a boundary test (p. 11-12). q3: ALE, ROE and THOA are non-learned; HPPO and HSAC are DRL methods applied to the same problem. q5 = 0: simulated scenarios and no code or data link.
